full_text: FICE 0) MARK GORDON STATE OF WYOMING EXECUTIVE DEPARTMENT EXECUTIVE ORDER Order 2020-1 WYOMING MULE DEER AND ANTELOPE MIGRATION CORRIDOR PROTECTION WHEREAS, Wyoming is home to the longest intact mule deer and antelope migration corridors in North America, and WHEREAS, migration corridors are essential to the maintenance of viable mule deer and antelope populations, and WHEREAS, wildlife that utilize these corridors are highly valued by all people and contribute significantly to the economy and reputation of Wyoming, and WHEREAS, land associated with migration corridors provide the state and nation with multiple- use opportunities that are integral to Wyoming's revenues, jobs, and way of life, and WHEREAS, private landowners play a key role in maintaining migration corridors, and WHEREAS, county governments play a significant role in land use planning and in conserving wildlife habitat and open spaces, and WHEREAS, all wildlife in Wyoming are property of the State and the Wyoming Game and Fish Department is charged with managing all of the State's wildlife in trust for the benefit of the citizens of the State and does so with a science-based approach, and NOW THEREFORE, to preclude any need for more regulatory action, or action by agencies beyond the purview of the State and without coordination with the State; pursuant to the authority vested in me by the Constitution and Laws of the State, and to the extent such actions are consistent with the statutory obligations and authority of each individual agency, including those tound in the Wyoming Regulatory Takings Act, Wyoming Statutes §§ 9-5-301 through 9- 5-305, L, Mark Gordon, Governor of the State of Wyoming, do hereby issue this Executive Order providing as follows: 200 WEST 24TH STREET CHEYENNE, WY 82002-0010 MARK GORDON GOVERNOR OF WYOMING 307.777.7434 • GOVERNOR@WYO.GOV HTTP://GOVERNOR.WYO.GOV ---PAGE--- Executive Order 2020-1 Wyoming Mule Deer and Antelope Migration Corridor Protection Page 2 of 5 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. 7. 8. 9. The Sublette Mule Deer, Baggs Mule Deer, and Platte Valley Mule Deer Migration Corridors are hereby designated (Appendix D). The process whereby other corridors could be designated in the future is established (Appendix B). Nothing in this Executive Order and the attached Appendices shall apply to actions taken by landowners on their private land or restrict state-issued permits a landowner seeks on his or her own land or minerals. Private landowners should be encouraged and incentivized to manage for the functionality of migration corridors. On privately-owned lands, for actions of a third-party developer requiring a state-issued permit, private landowners and the third-party developers are encouraged to finalize a surface-use agreement and to consult with the Wyoming Game and Fish Department (WGFD) concerning the permitted activities. Each executive branch agency in Wyoming shall exercise its legal and regulatory authorities to protect the annual movement of mule deer and antelope between seasonal ranges in their respective designated migration corridors. State agencies shall follow the procedures outlined in this Executive Order, while recognizing that adjustments to management may be necessary based upon local conditions, opportunities, and limitations (Appendix C). Where surface disturbance inside of designated corridors is proposed within, near, or adjacent to areas that have already been disturbed or are naturally unsuitable, state agencies should work to maintain habitat and minimize future disturbance by locating proposed disturbances within such disturbed or unsuitable areas (Appendix C). Subject to paragraphs 3 and 4 above, any surface-disturbing activities requiring a state- issued permit within designated corridors should be permitted in a manner that maintains the continued functionality of a designated migration corridor (Appendix C). Subject to paragraphs 3 and 4 above, any state-permitted activity within designated corridors during the migration period should be conditioned so as not to impede the functionality of the corridor by mule deer and antelope (Appendix C). Valid existing rights shall be recognized and respected. Existing activities will be conducted and conditioned as specified in the original authorizing permits or instruments) for such activities (Appendix E). ---PAGE--- 10. 11. 12. 13. 14. Executive Order 2020-1 Wyoming Mule Deer and Antelope Migration Corridor Protection Page 3 of 5 For recreational activities inside of designated migration corridors requiring a state permit, permitting agencies shall issue permits with the goal of maintaining migration corridor functionality, and minimizing impacts to animals using the designated corridor during migration periods. State agencies shall make comments for federally-issued recreation permits within designated corridors with the same goal (Appendix C). Boards of county commissioners may revise their land use plans to be consistent with this Executive Order. The State of Wyoming encourages this consideration and supports county governments should they develop a template for updating land-use plans consistent with this Executive Order. The Wyoming Department of Transportation (WyDOT), in conjunction with the Wyoming Game and Fish Department as well as other state agencies such as the Wyoming Wildlife and Natural Resource Trust, shall plan and engineer state and federal highway and associated projects that intersect designated migration corridors to avoid, minimize and mitigate vehicle/wildlife collisions, facilitate big game movement, and support migration connectivity to the extent practical. WyDOT shall include opportunities to address wildlife/roadway infrastructure projects in its annual planning efforts. This Executive Order is to be construed narrowly and limited to the habitat and activities specifically described herein. This Executive Order, together with its attachments, constitutes Wyoming's strategy for managing designated migration corridors and their habitats. Appendices to this Order are expressly adopted and incorporated by reference herein, and each shall have the full force and effect of this Executive Order. Amendment to any Appendix may be made without Given my hand and the Executive Seal of the State Of Wyoming this 13day of Zebruany Thank Sardar Mark Gordon Governor ---PAGE--- Executive Order 2020-1 Wyoming Mule Deer and Antelope Migration Corridor Protection Page 4 of 5 Appendix A Definitions Identified Migration Corridor: The geographic area used by big game for seasonal movements between summer and winter ranges that has undergone research by, or been approved by, the Wyoming Game and Fish Department (WGFD) to delineate the habitat and the components of habitat. Identified migration corridors are not subject to the management and processes outlined in this Executive Order, except as provided in Appendix B. Designated Migration Corridor: An identified mule deer or antelope migration corridor that was nominated for designation by the Wyoming Game and Fish Commission (WGFC) and was subject to the process for designation outlined in this Executive Order, including the Sublette Mule Deer, Baggs Mule Deer, and Platte Valley Mule Deer Corridors, which are formally designated by the signing of this Executive Order. High Use Area: Segment or portion of a mule deer and antelope migration corridor used by 20% or greater of the Global Position System (GPS)-collared animals. Medium Use Area: Segment or portion of a mule deer and antelope migration corridor used by 10-20% of the GPS-collared animals. Low Use Area: Segment or portion of a mule deer and antelope migration corridor used by less than 10% of the GPS-collared animals. Stopover Areas: The area used the majority of time by GPS-collared animals to forage and rest during spring and fall migration. Bottleneck: Any portion of a mule deer and antelope migration corridor where animals are significantly physically or behaviorally restricted. Biological Risk Assessment: Analyses of the potential biological risks, foreseeable biological threats, and conservation opportunities that exist in the migration corridor by the Wyoming Game and Fish Department. An assessment is developed with public stakeholder input and updated as conditions change on the landscape. Migration period: The specific dates during which migrating mule deer and antelope are physically present within a portion of a designated migration corridor, which can vary from year- to-year. Migration Corridor Functionality: Maintaining connectivity between summer and winter ranges to allow mule deer and antelope movements conducive to necessary foraging and rest during migration, based on the best-available scientific data. ---PAGE--- Executive Order 2020-1 Wyoming Muie Deer and Antelope Migration Corridor Protection Page 5 of 5 Appendix B Corridor Designation and Review Process Wyoming is home to numerous migration corridors. The identification of corridors may benefit herd management and overall herd fitness. It is the formal act of designating, rather than Identifying, a corridor that warrants limitations of human use to conserve those corridors. Not every migration corridor requires designation to ensure the health of the animals and/or the herd that uses it. The Wyoming Game and Fish Department (WGFD), as the agency with authority over the management of wildlife, shall lead research efforts on migration and identification of big game migration corridors. A summary of the results of WGFD research regarding migration corridors will be available to the public so long as the information is not 'sensitive wildlife location data within the meaning of Wyoming Statute § 16-4-203. A minimum of 3 years of research on a herd's migration patterns, which includes the collaring of a representative sample of animals from the herd, is necessary for a corridor to be considered for designation. The data gathered must be combined with scientifically-sound analysis techniques. Long-term knowledge of local WGFD personnel, landowners and other stakeholders is used in addition to this data to validate the identification of mule deer and antelope migration corridors, stopover areas, and mule deer and antelope migration bottlenecks. The WGFD will establish and utilize science-based criteria for determining whether an identified corridor necessitates consideration of designation. Prior to designation, any recommendation for the deferral of a mineral lease to the Bureau of Land Management or the Office of State Lands and Investments (OSLI) in an identified migration corridor shall be made at the sole discretion of the Governor, in consultation with WGFD, OSLI, and commissioners from the county or counties where the lease is located. The following process shall occur prior to any formal migration corridor designation: 1. WGFD identifies a migration corridor. During the initial identification, the following information shall be included in a publicly-available report: a. Mule deer or antelope pathway used to delineate the identified corridor and the underlying scientific information available that has informed the WGFD identification; b. The location, acreage, and land ownership of identified stopover areas; c. The location, acreage, and land ownership of identified bottlenecks; d. The location, acreage, and land ownership of identified high-use, medium- use, and low-use areas within the corridor; 2. If WGFD's initial report on an identified corridor determines designation may be warranted and the corridor meets established and publicly available criteria, the agency will develop a Biological Risk Assessment. Any assessment will be developed with appropriate county, state, ---PAGE--- Executive Order 2020-1 Wyoming Mule Deer and Antelope Migration Corridor Protection Page 6 of 5 and federal agency partners and updated as conditions warrant. The Biological Risk Assessment should not take more than 12 months to prepare and will involve public meetings in the region of the identified corridor. WGFD shall, consistent with its statutory authority, notify private landowners of identified migration corridors that intersect with that private landowner's property. 3. WGFD presents the identified corridor and Biological Risk Assessment to the Wyoming Game and Fish Commission (WGFC). 4. WGFC shall provide an opportunity for public comment regarding the identified corridor and the Biological Risk Assessment. 5. After considering the identified corridor, the Biological Risk Assessment, and public comment, the WGFC shall vote on whether to recommend to the Governor that an identified corridor be formally designated. 6. The Governor then determines if a designation will proceed. If the determination is made to proceed, the Governor will appoint an Area Working Group in consultation with the county commissioners representing any county through which an identified corridor passes, and if the corridor passes through the Wind River Indian Reservation, tribal representatives. Membership of the area working groups will include one county commissioner from each affected county, and if affected, a representative from the Eastern Shoshone and a representative from the Northern Arapaho Tribes. Other working group members will include up to seven individuals, at least two of whom will represent hunting, conservation, and wildlife, one will represent motorized outdoor recreation users, at least two of whom will represent agriculture, and at least two will represent industrial users including oil, gas, mining and renewable energy. All members of the Area Working Group will be appointed at the sole discretion of the Governor. Area Working Groups will meet in public and must complete their work in a timely manner. Their work will be completed in the timeframe specified by the Governor, and will be focused on those topics specified by the Governor including, but not limited to: WGFD's risk assessment, corridor components, potential impacts on socio-economic conditions of the region (jobs, county and state revenues, population, incomes, etc.), conservation opportunities, highway projects, and other tactors appropriate to the potential designation. They will also be directed to make recommendations on potential management after designation related to contested permits. These recommendations should take into consideration any county commission plans established to manage development inside the corridor as well as any BLM or Forest Service planning documents. 7. Final Area Working Group analysis and determination shall then be delivered to the Governor who either formally designates the identified corridor, returns the recommendation to WGFD for further refinement, or formally rejects the proposal for designation. ---PAGE--- Executive Order 2020-1 Wyoming Mule Deer and Antelope Migration Corridor Protection Page 7 of 5 8. In consultation with affected county commissioners and tribes, an Area Working Group of similar membership to that outlined above will be convened within five years of designation of a corridor. For the Sublette Mule Deer, Baggs Mule Deer, and Platte Valley Mule Deer Corridors the Governor will convene area working groups within two years. These groups will review the effectiveness of corridor designation on the migratory herd, opportunities for improved conservation, and evaluate the impacts of all restrictions on development and use of lands encompassed in the designated corridor. Each Area Working Group will report their findings to the Governor along with any other relevant recommendations. Appendix C New Infrastructure, Recreational Use and Development Conditions Wherever possible, development, infrastructure, and use should occur outside of designated corridors. Inside corridors, state regulatory agencies should support the continued functionality of designated migration corridors by conditioning permits to avoid and minimize impacts from development or use allowed within the corridor. Applicants for state-permitted projects and state-permitted uses within a designated migration corridor are required to consult with the Wyoming Game and Fish Department (WGFD) as part of the permitting process. After a consultation with the proponent, if the WGFD determines the proposed project or use will have adverse effects on migration corridor functionality the agency will work with the permit applicant to address these effects and provide recommendations to the proponent within five days. Permit applicants shall have access to all information considered in developing recommendations. Upon completion of that consultation, if the applicant does not agree with the recommendations of the WGFD it must prepare a letter outlining concerns with the WGFD recommendations. The WGFD will then deliver the recommendation and, if applicable, the accompanying letter to the Governor's Office within two days. The Governor shall review these materials and recommend a resolution of the applicant's concerns to the The following components of a corridor have unique management considerations for all development and uses: Bottlenecks: No surface disturbance or seasonal-human presence shall be permitted within bottlenecks, and state agencies shall restrict uses to those that do not impair migration corridor functionality, except in cases necessary for human safety. ---PAGE--- Executive Order 2020-1 Wyoming Mule Deer and Antelope Migration Corridor Protection Page 8 of 5 High Use Areas: Surface disturbance and human presence shall be limited to levels that maintain the corridor functionality and do not cause migrating mule deer or antelope to avoid or leave the high-use portion of the designated corridor during migration periods. Stopovers within High Use Areas: Within stopovers in high-use portions of the corridor, surface disturbance should be avoided. Permitted human activities during migration periods should be limited or avoided. Low and Medium Use Areas and Stopovers Within: Development and use can occur. Minimization, including project alterations, recreational permit restrictions, and other efforts that can be shown to reduce impacts to these areas should be considered where appropriate and will take into account whether an area is a low or medium use area. Surface disturbance, development and human presence during migration periods should be limited. Within low and medium use areas special consideration should be given to stopover areas to minimize disturbances. Federal leases, permits, rights of way, or other authorizations issued after designation of any corridor by the Governor should be issued to conform with the provisions of this Executive Order. State executive branch agencies will coordinate and cooperate with federal agencies and comment on federal agency actions in a manner that is consistent with this Executive Order. APPendix D Maps and specific shapefiles of of the three designated migration corridors are available at htps://wgld.wvo.gov/wildlife-in-wvoming/migration Appendix E Valid Existing Rights Within designated corridors existing rights shall be recognized and respected in furtherance of this Executive Order. Authorized activities, which are existing or permitted prior to the Governor's designation of a corridor are not subject to this Executive Order. Examples of existing activities include oil and gas development, mining, wind energy development, solar development, permitted recreational uses, transmission lines, processing facilities, state and federal highways, and other uses that were in place prior to the designation of the migration corridors and specific components of the corridors. full_text: STATE OF WYOMING EXECUTIVE DEPARTMENT EXECUTIVE ORDER Order 2020-1 (Reissued June 26, 2026 pursuant to Section 14) WYOMING MULE DEER AND ANTELOPE MIGRATION CORRIDOR PROTECTION WHEREAS, Wyoming is home to the longest intact mule deer and antelope migration corridors in North America, and WHEREAS, migration corridors are essential to the maintenance of viable mule deer and antelope populations, and WHEREAS, wildlife that utilize these corridors are highly valued by all people and contribute significantly to the economy and reputation of Wyoming, and WHEREAS, land associated with migration corridors provide the state and nation with multiple­ use opportunities that are integral to Wyoming's revenues,jobs, and way oflife, and WHEREAS, private landowners play a key role in maintaining migration corridors, and WHEREAS, county governments play a significant role in land use planning and in conserving wildlife habitat and open spaces, and WHEREAS, all wildlife in Wyoming are property of the State and the Wyoming Game and Fish Department is charged with managing all of the State's wildlife in trnst for the benefit of the citizens of the State and does so with a science-based approach, and NOW THEREFORE, to preclude any need for more regulatory action, or action by agencies beyond the purview of the State and without coordination with the State; pursuant to the authority vested in me by the Constitution and Laws of the State, and to the extent such actions are consistent with the statutory obligations and authority of each individual agency, including those found in the Wyoming Regulatory Takings Act, Wyoming Statutes§§ 9-5-301 through 9-5-305, I, Mark Gordon, Governor of the State of Wyoming, do hereby issue this Executive Order providing as follows: 200 WEST 24TH STREET CHEYENNE, WY 82002-0010 MARK GORDON GOVERNOR OF WYOMING 307.777.7434 • GOVERNOR@WYO.GOV HTTP://GOVERNOR.WYO.GOV Executive Order 2020-1 Wyoming Mule Deer and Antelope Migration Corridor Protection Page 2 of 5 I. The Sublette Mule Deer, Baggs Mule Deer, and Platte Valley Mule Deer Migration Corridors are hereby designated (Appendix D). 2. The process whereby other corridors could be designated in the future is established (Appendix B). 3. Nothing in this Executive Order and the attached Appendices shall apply to actions taken by landowners on their private land or restrict state-issued permits a landowner seeks on his or her own land or minerals. Private landowners should be encouraged and incentivized to manage for the functionality of migration conidors. 4. On privately-owned lands, for actions of a third-party developer requiring a state-issued permit, private landowners and the third-party developers are encouraged to finalize a surface-use agreement and to consult with ihe Wyoming Game and Fish Department (WGFD) concerning the permitted activities. 5. Each executive branch agency in Wyoming shall exercise its legal and regulatory authorities to protect the annual movement of mule deer and antelope between seasonal ranges in their respective designated migration corridors. State agencies shall follow the procedures outlined in this Executive Order, while recognizing that adjustments to management may be necessary based upon local conditions, opportunities, and limitations (Appendix C). 6. Where smface disturbance inside of designated corridors is proposed within, near, or adjacent to areas that have already been disturbed or are naturally unsuitable, state agencies should work to maintain habitat and minimize future disturbance by locating proposed disturbances within such disturbed or unsuitable areas (Appendix C). 7. Subject to paragraphs 3 and 4 above, any surface-disturbing activities requiring a state­ issued permit within designated c01Tidors should be permitted in a manner that maintains the continued functionality of a designated migration conidor (Appendix C). 8. Subject to paragraphs 3 and 4 above, any state-permitted activity within designated corridors during the migration period should be conditioned so as not to impede the functionality of the conidor by mule deer and antelope (Appendix C). 9. Valid existing rights shall be recognized and respected. Existing activities will be conducted and conditioned as specified in the original authorizing permits or instrument(s) for such activities (Appendix E).

However, under those licenses, alcoholic beverages are limited to on-premise consumption at the business; and WHEREAS, restaurants and bars & grills throughout the state, due to the emergency, are suffering severe economic deprivations which may be relieved by allowing these licensed businesses to offer alcoholic beverages for off -premise consumption; and WHEREAS, the State of Wyoming has the ability, through an executive order, to make emergency changes to the policies of the Liquor Division of the Wyoming Department of Revenue, so as to encourage economic stability through the operation of liquor licenses. full_text: HIS THA SHARK GORDON STATE OF WYOMING EXECUTIVE DEPARTMENT EXECUTIVE DEPARTMENT EXECUTIVE ORDER Order 2023-02 ESTABLISHMENT OF THE WYOMING CYBER ASSISTANCE RESPONSE EFFORT TEAM WHEREAS, due to the increasing involvement of technology in daily life, cybersecurity threats have become increasingly common and sophisticated, posing a significant risk to the security and well-being of Wyoming citizens and critical infrastructure; and WHEREAS, cyber-attacks on Wyoming's government agencies, businesses, critical infrastructure, and people can result in the theft of sensitive information, the disruption of essential services, and financial losses; and WHEREAS, these cyber-attacks can have severe consequences for Wyoming's economy and public safety, as well as potentially compromising national security; and WHEREAS, there are sixteen Critical Infrastructure Sectors, as defined by Presidential Policy Directive/PPD-21, whose systems, networks, and other assets are vital to the State of Wyoming's economy, safety, and well-being; and WHEREAS, any impairment or destruction of these assets, would have severe consequences for Wyoming's security, economic stability, public health, and safety; and WHEREAS, it is essential that Wyoming take proactive measures to prevent and respond to cybersecurity incidents; and WHEREAS, maintaining cybersecurity is a shared responsibility in which everyone has a critical role to play; and WHEREAS, effective prevention and responsiveness necessitates that state agencies, local governments, tribal governments, the private sector, academic institutions, and other 200 WEST 24TH STREET CHEYENNE, WY 82002-0010 MARK GORDON GOVERNOR OF WYOMING ---PAGE--- EO 2023-02 Establishment of the Wyoming Cyber Assistance Response Page 2 relevant entities exercise due diligence in mitigating cyber risks through coordinated information sharing, monitoring, and incident response; and WHEREAS, it is vital to marshal the resources and expertise needed to combat these threats and defend Wyoming's digital frontier, including the establishment of a Cyber Assistance Response Effort (CARE) Team; NOW, THEREFORE, pursuant to the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of Wyoming, I, Governor Mark Gordon, do hereby order and direct: 1. The Wyoming Cyber Assistance Response Effort (CARE) Team is hereby established. 2. The mission of the CARE Team is to protect Wyoming and its institutions by reducing the impacts of cyber-related events, including incidents and disruptions, through prevention, response, and recovery. This Executive Order provides a framework that enables the state emergency management and information technology to work seamlessly with state, local, tribal, private sector, and other relevant partners to rapidly respond to and minimize the impact of cyber events in Wyoming. 3. Members of the CARE Team shall include, but are not limited to, at least one representative from each of the following entities: a. The Wyoming Office of the Chief Information Officer and Enterprise Technology Services (ETS); b. The Wyoming Information Analysis Team; c. The Wyoming Division of Criminal Investigation's Computer Crime Team; d. The Wyoming Office of Homeland Security; and e. The Wyoming National Guard. 4. The Wyoming Office of Homeland Security (WOHS) shall lead the CARE Team and shall determine the frequency of its meetings. 200 WEST 24TH STREET CHEYENNE, WY 82002-0010 MARK GORDON GOVERNOR OF WYOMING ---PAGE--- EO 2023-02 Establishment of the Wyoming Cyber Assistance Response Page 3 5. The CARE Team shall review cybersecurity and other technology-based threat information and assess vulnerabilities, and present their findings and recommendations for the protection of State resources to the Governor's Office. 6. The CARE Team shall continuously review, update, and implement the Wyoming Cyber Disruption Response Plan. As updates to the plan are made, the CARE Team shall submit the plan to the Governor's Office for review and approval. This plan provides a common framework for identifying and responding to technological threats that mirrors the federal government model, with corresponding responses to address threats of increasing scope and severity. 7. All Wyoming state agencies shall report known or suspected cybersecurity incidents to ETS immediately upon detection. ETS shall carry out the following functions: a. Pursuant to Wyo. Stat. Ann. §§ 9-2-2901 through -2906, ETS is responsible for working with state agencies managing security risks. This includes managing information security policies and standards, working with agencies on technical matters, and ensuring enterprise projects meet security requirements. b. ETS, in cooperation with CARE Team members and other subject matter experts, shall investigate all state agency reports of cybersecurity incidents. c. ETS will decide on behalf of state agencies in determining the appropriate reactive measures to a cyber event and shall regularly and promptly notify the CARE Team members of such events, event details, and response efforts. 8. The CARE Team will create partnerships that help protect Wyoming Critical Infrastructure and Key Resources, as that term is defined by the United States Department of Homeland Security. This includes the following actions: a. The CARE Team shall seek to work and partner with relevant federal agencies including the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), the Cybersecurity Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), the Federal Bureau 200 WEST 24TH STREET HEYENNE, WY 82002-001 MARK GORDON GOVERNOR OF WYOMING 307.777.7434 • GOVERNOR@WYO.GOV HTTP://GOVERNOR.WYO.GOV ---PAGE--- EO 2023-02 Establishment of the Wyoming Cyber Assistance Response Page 4 of Investigation (FBI), and the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA). b. The CARE Team shall seek to work and partner with Wyoming public and private sector Critical Infrastructure and Key Resources (CIKR) partners. The CARE Team shall also work to establish a cooperative environment of information sharing between the CARE Team and public and private CIKR partners for the purpose of threat mitigation, response, and recovery. c. Use the forgoing directives and authorization to implement a continuous improvement process to enhance, improve and harden Wyoming and its institutions against cybersecurity threats and events. full_text: MARK GORDON STATE OF WYOMING EXECUTIVE DEPARTMENT EXECUTIVE ORDER Order 2024-05 Correcting and Rescinding Executive Order No. 2024-04 ESTABLISHMENT OF THE WYOMING HEALTHCARE WORKFORCE TASK FORCE WHEREAS, Wyoming is a rural and geographically expansive state, blessed with wide open spaces and incredible natural beauty; WHEREAS, Wyoming citizens reasonably expect, and deserve, access to high quality healthcare services as close to home as possible; WHEREAS, the rural, sometimes isolated, nature of Wyoming's communities can make it difficult to ensure adequate access to high quality healthcare services; WHEREAS, Wyoming has many quality healthcare professionals and facilities, all of which strive to provide the best care possible to Wyoming citizens; WHEREAS, despite the best intentions and hard work of these professionals and facilities, the state is plagued by chronic workforce shortages and limitations on access to healthcare; WHEREAS, the shortage of quality healthcare professionals in Wyoming results in decreased access to care including longer wait times, greater distances to access care, and increased costs for receiving care; WHEREAS, Wyoming healthcare licensing requirements, while properly intended to protect the citizens of the state, may also create unnecessary delays and barriers that can be streamlined; WHEREAS, professional educational program requirements might be better aligned and enhanced between our educational institutions for easy transitions into higher educational programs in healthcare; and WHEREAS, while Wyoming healthcare professionals may have specific skills for supporting patients, health insurance payors may not cover certain services, thus disincentivizing the provision of needed healthcare specialties. 200 WEST 24TH STREET CHEYENNE, WY 82002-0010 MARK GORDON GOVERNOR OF WYOMING 307.777.7434 • GOVERNOR@WYO.GOV HTTP://GOVERNOR.WYO.GOV ---PAGE--- March 8, 2024 Correcting and Rescinding Executive Order No. 2024-04 Page 2 NOW, THEREFORE, pursuant to the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of Wyoming, I, Governor Mark Gordon, do hereby order and direct: 1. The Wyoming Healthcare Workforce Task Force (the "Task Force") shall be created and composed of no more than thirty (30) members appointed by the Governor from the following entities: a. Wyoming healthcare licensing boards, b. The Wyoming Department of Workforce Services, c. The University of Wyoming and Wyoming community colleges, d. Wyoming health insurance payors, e. The Wyoming Department of Administration and Information, f. The Wyoming Department of Health, g. Appropriate non-governmental and other industry organizations, and h. A representative of the Governor's Office. 2. Of the members appointed to the Task Force, the Governor will appoint seven (7) members to serve on an executive committee. The Governor will also appoint an administrator responsible for facilitating meetings and communications for the Task Force. 3. The mission of the Task Force will be to investigate and develop recommendations to (1) remove barriers to healthcare licensing, (2) establish healthcare professional educational pipelines with stackable credentialing, and (3) coordinate with Wyoming health insurance payors for coverage of pipeline professionals. 4. Develop any internal bylaws and operating procedures as necessary to carry out the duties described in this Order; c. Review available data and reports; d. Collaborate and engage with necessary stakeholders in carrying out its duties under this Order; e. Develop and submit to the Governor, by June 30, 2024, the following: i. A list of key recommendations for removing barriers to healthcare ii. licensing in Wyoming; An educational pipeline strategic plan, incorporating industry input, that includes, but is not limited to, the expansion of programming, new programming, and other alternatives to ensure a Wyoming student can reach the highest level of professional degree or certification in Wyoming; and; ili. and WHEREAS, during the 2024 legislative session, the Governor vetoed Section 307 and Section 310 of the 2024 Wyoming Session Laws, Ch. 118 (the "2024 Budget Bill"), and the legislature did not override these vetoes; and WHEREAS, Section 307 and Section 310 of the 2024 Budget Bill infringe upon the separation of powers amongst the three branches of state government required under Article 2, Section 1 of the Wyoming Constitution; and WHEREAS, as indicated in his line item veto message, in addition to the constitutional concerns, the Governor vetoed Section 307 and Section 310 of the 2024 Budget Bill to provide flexibility to the executive branch to efficiently and effectively address unforeseen challenges in executing the law, allocating resources, and fulfilling duties charged by the legislature; and WHEREAS, as indicated in his March 22, 2024 line item veto message, the Governor stated that the executive branch would implement measures to prevent unchecked growth in positions and budgets, and to administer Wyoming's funds in a fiscally responsible manner; NOW, THEREFORE, pursuant to the authority vested in me by the Constitution and by the laws of the State of Wyoming, I, Mark Gordon, do hereby order that the Department of Administration and Information, the State Budget Department, and any other applicable state 200 WEST 24TH STREET CHEYENNE, WY 82002-0010 MARK GORDON GOVERNOR OF WYOMING 307.777.7434 • GOVERNOR@WYO.GOV HTTP://GOVERNOR.WYO.GOV ---PAGE--- EO 2024-07 Budget Funds For Personal Services Page 2 agency shall promulgate rules and/or adopt policies and procedures to reflect the following limitations and restrictions regarding 100 series and 900 series appropriated funds: 1. Stat. Ann. § 22-3-102, require every person to be at least eighteen (18) years old and a citizen of the United States, before they can legally register for and vote in our elections; and WHEREAS, people who entered the United States illegally and have failed to lawfully become U.S. citizens have no right to vote in Wyoming elections and should not be allowed to influence our elections; and WHEREAS, pursuant to Wyoming's election code, including Wyo. Stat. Ann. §§ 22-3-102 through -106 and -116, Wyoming's County Clerks and the Secretary of State already actively work to validate voter registration information and investigate, verify, challenge, and deny registration to non-citizens; and WHEREAS, Article 4, Sections 1 and 4 of the Wyoming Constitution vest executive power in the Governor and charge him with ensuring Wyoming laws are faithfully executed; NOW THEREFORE, 1, Mark Gordon, Governor of the State of the State of Wyoming, to the full extent of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of Wyoming do hereby issue this Executive Order providing as follows: 200 WEST 24TH STREET CHEYENNE, WY 82002-0010| MARK GORDON GOVERNOR OF WYOMING 307.777.7434 • GOVERNOR@WYO.GOV HTTP://GOVERNOR.WYO.GOV| ---PAGE--- EO 2024-11 Preserving the Integrity of Wyoming Elections Page 2 1. State agencies entering into or renewing contracts with federal agencies or partners must confirm there is no requirement to provide voter registration materials to non-citizens or otherwise requiring voter registration activities for non-citizens. C. State agencies under my authority will expeditiously report any suspected instances of non-citizen voting that they may encounter in the course of carrying out their statutorily mandated duties to the appropriate authorities immediately. 2. Further, I encourage the Secretary of State and the County Clerks to continue to effectively and efficiently use the tools provided to each of them by Wyoming's election code to investigate and verify voter registration in order to preserve Wyoming's proud legacy of successful, well-executed, and secure elections. full_text: OF THE MARIK GORDON STATE OF WYOMING EXECUTIVE DEPARTMENT EXECUTIVE ORDER Order 2025 -04 INCREASE OF ACTIVE FOREST MANAGEMENT IN WYOMING WHEREAS, the recent Executive Order 14225 signed by President Trump concerning the expansion of timber management is an essential solution to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfires that impact Wyoming's communities, natural resources and watersheds; and WHEREAS, the recent Secretary Memorandum 1078-006, Increasing Timber Production and Designating an Emergency Situation on National Forest System Lands directs the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Forest Service (USFS) to increase active forest management by reducing barriers and focusing on necessary efficiencies; and WHEREAS, forty-eight percent of Wyoming's lands are federally owned, with the majority of Wyoming's forests located on federal lands; and WHEREAS, wildfire and forest health threats do not recognize boundaries, and fires that start on federal lands can become major threats to lives, property, water supply and storage, wildlife habitat, recreation and tourism, and more; and WHEREAS, Congress has enacted laws that increase the pace and scale of active forest management that can be enhanced by cross-boundary vegetation projects; and WHEREAS, Wyoming's forests hold values beyond simple monetary measurements and deserve investments to protect and maintain those values, which include managing timber resources for wide-scale utilization. and WHEREAS, since 2017, the Good Neighbor Authority (GNA) has served as an important instrument to increase forest vegetation project work across USFS and Bureau of Land Management (BLM) lands in Wyoming through timber harvesting, thinning, fuels mitigation projects, wildlife restoration work, and coordinated invasive weed control efforts; and WHEREAS, Wyoming State Forestry Division (WSFD) is successfully implementing the GNA program with the USFS and BLM Wyoming Office concerning BLM federal lands, and are 200 WEST 24TH STREET CHEYENNE, WY 82002-0010 MARK GORDON GOVERNOR OF WYOMING 307.777.7434 • GOVERNOR@WYO.GOV HTTP://GOVERNOR.WYO.GOV ---PAGE--- EO 2025-04 Increase Active Forest Management in Wyoming Page 2 expanding these partnerships to include other federal lands such as the Department of Interior Bureau of Reclamation and National Park Service lands; and WHEREAS, WSFD also partners with the USDA Natural Resource Conservation Service (NRCS), Wyoming's County Commissioners, and Wyoming's Conservation Districts to increase the pace and scale of crucial cross-boundary management on two million acres of forested private lands; full_text: STATE OF WYOMING EXECUTIVE DEPARTMENT EXECUTIVE ORDER Order 2022-01 EMERGENCY EXEMPTION FROM PERMISSIBLE OPERATING TIME REGULATIONS WHEREAS, the people of the State of Wyoming are faced with low supplies of propane with which to heat their homes and businesses and carry out commerce due to cold temperatures in the region; and WHEREAS, it is necessary for propane customers throughout the State of Wyoming to receive deliveries quickly in the face of high levels of use created by the exceptionally cold conditions; and WHEREAS, regulatory impediments to the expeditious delivery of propane to customers throughout Wyoming threaten to endanger the health and welfare of the people; and WHEREAS, drivers of propane delivery vehicles are required to deliver supplies of this product in order to meet this demand for the product; and WHEREAS, the State of Wyoming has the ability, through an executive order, to make emergency changes in regulations so that the prompt delivery of propane to customers throughout the state is not impeded by restrictions to the hours that can be worked by qualified drivers; and WHEREAS, in the interest of public safety, the Wyoming Legislature, in Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 31- 18-303(a), has mandated that the Wyoming Department of Transportation adopt rules and regulations prescribing the permissible operating time and other requirements of motor carrier drivers, and the Department has complied with this mandate by adopting its own rules of motor carriers, chapter 1, § 9, which requires compliance with various federal regulations, including 49 CFR 390 and 49 CFR 395 of the United States Department of Transportation Motor Carrier Safety Regulations; and WHEREAS, 49 CFR 390.23 permits a state official authorized to declare an emergency, such as the Governor of the State of Wyoming, in the event of such declaration, to exempt motor carrier drivers from certain regulations, including operating time requirements. EO 2022-01 Emergency Exemption From Permissible Operating Time Regulations Page 2 NOW, THEREFORE, pursuant to the authority vested in me by the Constitution and by the laws of the State of Wyoming, I, Mark Gordon, do hereby order and direct: 1. A state of emergency exists in Wyoming, and I hereby declare such an emergency. The emergency requires that the transportation and delivery of propane into and within the State of Wyoming shall be exempt from 49 CFR 395.3. 2. Nothing contained in this Order shall be construed as an exemption from the controlled substances, alcohol use, and testing requirements (49 CFR 382), the commercial driver's license requirements (49 CFR 383), the financial responsibility requirements (49 CFR 387), applicable size and weight requirements, or any other portion of the regulations not specifically identified in this Order. 3. Propane transportation or delivery companies, while under this Order, shall not require or allow any fatigued driver to operate a propane delivery vehicle. A driver who informs a carrier that he/she needs immediate rest shall be given adequate rest before the driver is required to return to service. Be it further ordered, this Executive Order is effective immediately and shall expire upon the conclusion of the emergency, but no later than midnight, February 7, 2022. Given under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Wyoming this 7th day of January, 2022. __________________________ Mark Gordon Governor

full_text: SAT GORDON STATE OF WYOMING EXECUTIVE DEPARTMENT EXECUTIVE ORDER Order 2025-07 MAKING WYOMING HEALTHY AGAIN ENHANCING NUTRITION IN THE SUPPLEMENTAL NUTRITION ASSISTANCE PROGRAM WHEREAS, pursuant to Executive Order 14212, "Establishing the President's Make America Healthy Again Commission," signed by President Donald J. Trump on February 13, 2025, the President acknowledged the current health crisis facing the United States, and announced the policy of the United States Government to "aggressively combat the critical health challenges facing our citizens," including childhood chronic diseases caused by an inadequate diet; WHEREAS, the federal Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program ("SNAP") is administered by the Wyoming Department of Family Services ("DFS) to provide food assistance and a nutritious diet to lower-income Wyomingites under the umbrella of the United States Department of Agriculture ("USDA"); WHEREAS, the SNAP program plays a critical role in combating food insecurity and promoting the well-being of residents across Wyoming; WHEREAS, the reach and impact of Wyoming's SNAP program are substantial, serving a significant portion of the state's population. As of October 7, 2025, the program provides essential food assistance to approximately 12,700 households, which includes over 26,000 individuals of varying ages from elderly to infant, employed, partially employed, or others who count on the program to meet basic healthy nutritional requirements, the majority of whom are children and the elderly; WHEREAS, food items such as sweetened beverages and candy contain significant amounts of high fructose corn syrup or sugar that provide no nutritional value for a healthy diet; WHEREAS, a poor nutritional diet can lead to various health problems, including chronic diseases like obesity, type 2 diabetes, and heart disease, as well as weakened immune function and poor mental health; WHEREAS, compelling statistics from the American Diabetes Association indicate that over thirty percent (30%) of adults in Wyoming are classified as obese, a significant public health concern with widespread implications, and concurrently, approximately nine and one-half 200 WEST 24TH STREET CHEYENNE, WY 82002-0010 MARK GORDON GOVERNOR OF WYOMING 307.777.7434 • GOVERNOR@WYO.GOV HTTP://GOVERNOR.WYO.GOV ---PAGE--- EO 2025-07 Making Wyoming Healthy Again Page 2 percent (9.5%) of adults in Wyoming are living with diabetes. These figures underscore a clear and pressing need within the state to promote and facilitate the adoption of healthy and nutritious dietary practices among its citizens to mitigate the escalating health burden associated with these preventable conditions; WHEREAS, the health and vitality of Wyoming's residents are paramount, serving as the bedrock upon which strong and thriving communities are built. When individuals and families are healthy, they are better equipped to succeed in all facets of life, whether in the workplace, educational institutions, or within their homes; WHEREAS, it is in the best interest of the State of Wyoming to proactively encourage and incentivize healthy lifestyle choices for its citizens. This includes implementing measures designed to reduce the consumption of unhealthy food items, such as sweetened beverages and candy, that are known contributors to prevalent health problems such as obesity, diabetes, and a host of other serious health concerns. By fostering an environment that supports healthier eating, Wyoming can significantly improve the quality of life for its residents and reduce the long-term healthcare burden on the State; WHEREAS, USDA allows states to apply for waivers to exclude certain food items from the federal SNAP program as administered by the state; however, such waivers can introduce complexities in the administration and implementation of the SNAP program. These complexities and challenges include, without limitation, carefully identifying restricted food items so that no anomalies occur and ensuring that retailers are not overly burdened by the cost and complexity in implementing the waiver resulting in a reduction in the number of retailers participating in Wyoming's SNAP program; WHEREAS, USDA calculates the error rate of a state's implementation of its SNAP program and a higher error rate can significantly shift a portion of the cost of the SNAP program from the federal government to the state; and WHEREAS, through the dedication and competence of its employees DFS has always maintained one of the lowest error rates in the nation in its implementation of Wyoming's SNAP program, and it is critical to maintain this low error rate so that Wyoming will not be subject to increased cost burden of its SNAP program; NOW, THEREFORE, pursuant to the authority vested in me by the laws of the State of Wyoming, I, Mark Gordon, do hereby order and direct the following: 1. DFS shall conduct an examination of food items with no or low nutritional value, such as soft drinks, other sweetened beverages and candy. Upon completion of its review, DFS shall recommend those food items to be excluded from Wyoming's SNAP program (the "Excluded Items") and DFS shall prepare a plan containing all elements necessary to apply for a waiver to exclude those items from eligible foods as defined in 7 U.S.C. § 2012(k) and 7 C.F.R. § 271.2. DFS shall present this plan to me for my approval no later than January 2, 2026 and shall file the waiver with USDA no later than January 7, 2026. 200 WEST 24TH STREET CHEYENNE, WY 82002-0010 MARK GORDON GOVERNOR OF WYOMING 307.777.7434 • GOVERNOR@WYO.GOV HTTP://GOVERNOR.WYO.GOV ---PAGE--- EO 2025-07 Making Wyoming Healthy Again Page 3 2. Understanding the complexity involved in implementing and administering changes to the SNAP program, DFS may consider a plan that restricts the Excluded Items in steps or phases so that changes to the program are implemented in a manner that ensures accuracy and efficiency. Factors to be considered by DFS when preparing the plan for the waiver include, without limitation, the potential impact to Wyoming's error rate in the administration of the SNAP waiver, the difficulty of retailers to implement the waiver and the potential of lost access to healthy foods if retailers no longer participate in the program, especially in Wyoming's most rural areas, and the additional administration costs associated with the implementation and administration of the waiver. 3. The DFS Director will coordinate and consult with key stakeholders, such as public health and nutrition experts, SNAP beneficiaries and administrators, related business and industry representatives and other appropriate state agencies, in the preparation of the waiver plan to be submitted to USDA. 4. Should this waiver be granted, the Director of DFS shall prohibit the purchase of the Excluded Items with SNAP benefits provided through the SNAP program in compliance with the terms and conditions of such waiver. 5. The Director of DFS shall provide monthly progress reports on the application for, and implementation of, the SNAP waiver to the Governor until the directives in this Executive Order have been fully implemented. 6. All departments, commissions, boards and agencies, and officers of the State, or any political subdivision therein, are authorized and directed to cooperate in the implementation of this Executive Order. This Executive Order is effective October 31, 2025 and shall remain in effect until amended or repealed. full_text: OMING GOVERNO MATK GORDON STATE OF WYOMING EXECUTIVE DEPARTMENT EXECUTIVE ORDER Order 2025-08 DECLARATION OF PUBLIC WELFARE EMERGENCY WHEREAS, the federal government typically provides Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program ("SNAP") benefits to low-income Wyomingites through discretionary spending. On September 19, 2025, 11 days prior to the expiration of federal appropriations, the U.S. House of Representatives passed a clean continuing resolution ("CR") to extend federal discretionary spending. Senate Democrats, however, refused to vote for the CR as many as 13 times since the House passed it. Due to the Democrat-imposed lapse in funding, SNAP will likely exhaust its resources as soon as November 1, 2025 and thus be unable to provide benefits to Wyomingites. WHEREAS, over 26,000 Wyomingites count on SNAP benefits to meet ordinary healthy nutritional needs. The Governor of the State of Wyoming, Mark Gordon, recognizes food banks and churches in Wyoming are currently not equipped to fully handle the impacts of SNAP benefits evaporating in the wake of the Democrat Shutdown. The Governor acknowledges hunger is not a partisan issue - food insecurity does not differentiate between Republican or Democrat, and Wyoming will not allow our citizens experiencing food insecurity to be held hostage or used for leverage. WHEREAS, the statutes of the State of Wyoming, particularly Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 9-2-1014.3, confer upon the Governor of the State of Wyoming the authority to expend up to ten million dollars ($10,000,000.00) from the legislative stabilization reserve account in the event of a public welfare emergency. Under Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 9-2-1002(a)(xxv), a public welfare emergency is "a sudden financial calamity or other occurrence... [that] (A) [w]as not foreseeable or predictable at the time of the adoption of the budget, ... [that] (B) [dJemands immediate action to insure the proper functioning of state government or to protect the health, safety or welfare or economic well-being of the public or against the loss of essential public services; and (C) [flor which other funds are not available for expenditure or insufficient to meet the needs of the emergency." WHEREAS, the Governor finds that the discontinuation of SNAP funds constitutes a sudden financial calamity or occurrence, which was not foreseeable at the time of preparation and adoption of the state's current budget. The Governor also finds that the discontinuation of SNAP funds demands immediate action to protect the health, welfare and economic well-being of the public. Finally, the Governor finds that other funds are not available to meet the needs of this emergency. 200 WEST 24TH STREET CHEYENNE, WY 82002-0010 MARK GORDON GOVERNOR OF WYOMING 307.777.7434 • GOVERNOR@WYO.GOV HTTP://GOVERNOR.WYO.GOV ---PAGE--- EO 2025-08 Declaration of Public Welfare Emergency Page 2 NOW, THEREFORE, pursuant to the authority vested in me by the laws of the State of Wyoming, I, Mark Gordon, do hereby declare a public welfare emergency. I therefore order and direct the following: 1. The Director of the Wyoming Department of Family Services to coordinate with the Wyoming State Budget Director and use the aforementioned emergency funds to support appropriate charitable organizations and churches which have food banks, pantries, and mobile food pantries in providing food consistent with SNAP approved items for Wyoming citizens until the Democrat Shutdown comes to an end. 2. Aligned with the intent of promoting healthier food for Wyomingites expressed in Governor's Executive Order 2025-07, the Director of Family Services will provide grant agreements to those receiving funds and direct that they use reasonable efforts to purchase nutritional, healthy food with the distributed funds. 3. The Director of the Wyoming Department of Family Services to submit a proposed emergency hunger relief program to provide week-to-week distribution of funds. 4. The Director of the Department of Family Services will submit the proposal to the Governor's Office for approval no later than November 1, 2025. Given under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Wyoming this 31st day of October, 2025. WHEREAS, ensuring and maintaining public trust in the work of government is vital to the long-term stability of our state and Republic. WHEREAS, pursuant to Wyo. Stat. § 8-3-123(ix) and (x), the State Code of Wyoming encourages Wyomingites to "[r]emember that some things are not for sale" and to "[k]now where to draw the line." WHEREAS, it is important that state facilities are only used for the work of state government and that state funded resources like state buildings and offices are not used for political or campaign activities. Stat. § 9-5-106(a), the "state building commission is authorized to adopt rules and regulations relative to the operation, management, and use of any state leased or owned building." The following conditions shall apply to such emergency relief permits: 1. Oversize loads of livestock feed may be transported over any state highway in the state of Wyoming two (2) hours before official sunrise to two (2) hours after official sunset. 2. Vehicles hauling oversize loads of livestock feed on any state highway are not to exceed twelve (12) feet six (6) inches in width, or fifteen (15) feet in height. "Oversize Load" signs (front and rear) are required. 3. For non-daylight travel, vehicles hauling oversize loads of livestock feed shall be equipped with amber clearance lights on each front corner, and a red clearance light on each rear corner of the load or vehicle (whichever is wider). Such loads shall also display a revolving amber light, amber strobe light, or two-way flashing amber lights at least four (4) inches in diameter on the vehicle. LED assemblies meeting the visibility requirements shall be allowed. These lights shall be clearly visible at least one thousand (1,000) feet from the front and rear of the vehicle. 4. Vehicles hauling overweight loads of livestock feed or livestock exclusive of interstate highways shall be at a weight which is not more than ten percent (10%) in excess of allowed axle weights and not more than five thousand (5,000) pounds in excess gross weight allowed under Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 31-18-802(a)(vi), Gross Weight Table I. 5. This Executive Order does not grant authority for any vehicle to exceed Class F weight limits or posted bridge and road limits of any such road. 6. The permits are only valid for movements of livestock feed or livestock to either a destination within Wyoming or through Wyoming to a destination in another state that has declared an emergency for livestock feed or livestock.
